title: Behavioral Mock Round
oneLiner: Random questions in Amazon, Google, Meta or general style, a timer, likely follow-ups, and a checklist to grade yourself.
keyTakeaway: Practise out loud with a timer. Answers that read well in your head run long and lose their structure when spoken, and the follow-up questions ("what would you do differently?", "what did your manager think?") are where interviewers find out whether the story holds up.
explanation:
Pick a company style and a round length. You get questions one at a time, chosen to cover different competencies the way a real loop spreads them across interviewers. For each one, choose which of your stories you'd tell, start the timer, and answer out loud. Recording yourself on your phone helps a lot; you'll hear every "um" and every minute spent on background.

When you've finished, the round shows what the interviewer is listening for and the follow-ups they'd probably ask. Answer those too, then tick the checklist honestly. At the end you'll see your times, which checklist items you missed most, and which competencies your story bank doesn't cover yet.

Company styles differ. Amazon ties every question to a Leadership Principle, each interviewer owns a few principles, and the follow-ups dig hard into data and your personal role. Google's "Googleyness and leadership" round mixes past-behaviour questions with hypotheticals about ambiguity and teamwork. Meta's behavioral round focuses on impact, conflict and growth, and the scope of your stories helps decide the level you're hired at. The "Any company" set covers what nearly everyone asks.
